goals.name: Reduce nutrients and sediment and meet TMDL load allocations

goals.name: Vision: improve and/or protect water quality in streams and creeks
goals.description: The implementation team's vision is an outcome statement about improving or protecting water quality in the watershed's streams and creeks.
goals.targetText: improve and/or protect the quality of water in streams and creeks
goals.sourceQuote: improve and/or protect the quality of water in streams and creeks.

goals.name: Reduce agricultural nutrient and sediment loading and stabilize creeks
goals.description: This goal targets nutrient and sediment loads from agricultural lands and aims to return the creeks from unstable to stable stream levels so that they could meet water quality standards.

goals.sourceQuote: The goal and objective is to reduce the nutrient and sediment loading coming from agricultural

goals.name: Remove impaired segments of Muddy Creek from the 303(d) list
goals.description: The desired result of the project is to reduce nutrient loading to acceptable levels and to delist the impaired segments of Muddy Creek.

goals.sourceQuote: The desired benefit of this project will be the reduction of nutrient loading to levels that are

goals.name: 45 to 70% reduction of nonpoint source nutrient loads to Muddy Creek
goals.description: This is the load reduction recommended by the nutrients/low DO/organic enrichment TMDL. The plan commits to meeting the TMDL allocations, so this serves as its numeric target.
goals.targetText: 45 to 70% reduction of the nutrient loads entering Muddy Creek from nonpoint sources
goals.sourceQuote: includes a 45 to 70% reduction of the nutrient loads entering Muddy Creek from nonpoint sources.

goals.name: Attain preliminary nutrient target range of 0.6mg/l to 0.11mg/l
goals.description: The funded proposal states that the TMDL nutrient reduction is intended to attain a preliminary in-stream target concentration range.
goals.sourceQuote: The TMDL recommends a 45 to 70% reduction in the amount of nutrients from nonpoint sources entering Muddy Creek to attain the preliminary target range of 0.6mg/l to 0.11mg/l.

goals.name: Reduce soil loss on pasture land
goals.description: This is an additional project objective in the funded proposal: reduce soil loss from pasture land in the watershed and thereby reduce sediment entering Muddy Creek.
goals.targetText: reduce soil loss on pasture land in the watershed
goals.sourceQuote: Another objective of this project will be to reduce soil loss on pasture land in the watershed.

bmps.name: Streambank and Shoreline Protection
bmps.description: Bank protection funded under the 319 grant to reduce sediment and attached nutrients entering Bell Creek and Muddy Creek from eroding banks.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Grade Stabilization Structure
bmps.description: Structures to stop gully and head-cut erosion on agricultural land, reducing sediment and nutrient loading. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Pasture and Hay Land Planting
bmps.description: Establishing pasture and hay cover on erosive sloping land to reduce sheet erosion and nutrient runoff. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)
bmps.sourceQuote: Pasture and Hay Land Planting |  |  |  | 100 acres | $200/ac | $20,000

bmps.name: Water and Sediment Control Basin
bmps.description: Small basins that trap runoff and sediment from agricultural fields to cut sediment and nutrient loads. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)
bmps.sourceQuote: Water and Sediment Control Basin |  |  |  |  | 4 structures | $10,000/ ea | $40,000

bmps.name: Nutrient Management
bmps.description: Nutrient management on agricultural acres to reduce nutrient loads toward the TMDL's 45-70% nonpoint nutrient reduction. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Tank/Trough
bmps.description: Livestock watering tanks or troughs that provide alternative water away from streams, reducing animal waste and nutrient inputs. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Diversions
bmps.description: Diversions that redirect runoff to control erosion and reduce sediment delivery from agricultural land. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Heavy Use Area Protection
bmps.description: Stabilizing livestock heavy use areas to reduce erosion and runoff of animal waste and nutrients. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Fencing
bmps.description: Fencing to manage cattle and limit animal access to streams, addressing nutrient and sediment inputs. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Critical Area Planting
bmps.description: Vegetating highly erosive critical areas to reduce sediment and attached nutrient losses. Funded under the 319 project.
bmps.location: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed (agricultural lands in Tippah County)

bmps.name: Stream Crossings
bmps.description: Stream crossings are listed among the practices in the watershed management action plan table. They are not part of the funded 319 budget.

outreach.responsibleParty: Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission, MDEQ, Tippah County SWCD
outreach.sourceQuote: Presentations relating to water quality will be made to civic organizations.

outreach.name: Radio Advertisements
outreach.description: Spots on the local radio station informing people about water quality and nonpoint source pollution.
outreach.responsibleParty: Mississippi Soil and Water Conservation Commission, MDEQ, Tippah County SWCD
outreach.sourceQuote: Radio advertisements will be run on the local radio station to inform people about water quality and nonpoint source pollution. Each spot will run 5 times a days for 2 weeks.

outreach.name: Adopt-A-Stream workshop
outreach.description: An Adopt-A-Stream stewardship workshop for the watershed covering stream health, ecology and water chemistry, with participants tracked.
outreach.responsibleParty: Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality and Mississippi Wildlife Federation
outreach.sourceQuote: At least one event will take place before September 30, 2014.

outreach.name: Stakeholder notification for plan evaluation
outreach.description: During plan evaluation, WIT members notify their stakeholders that they can propose changes to the plan, with one month allowed for notification.
outreach.timeframe: Every three to five years or as needed
outreach.sourceQuote:
The WIT members will be responsible for notifying

their stakeholders of the opportunity to propose changes to the watershed implementation plan.

geographicAreas.name: Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed
geographicAreas.description: The subwatershed of Muddy Creek in Tippah County that the plan targets for BMP implementation.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Subwatershed is an 19,277 acre subwatershed.

geographicAreas.name: Muddy Creek Watershed
geographicAreas.description: The larger watershed that contains the Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Watershed. Muddy Creek has fecal coliform and nutrient/low DO TMDLs.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The Muddy Creek watershed is approximately 63,682 acres.

geographicAreas.name: HUC 08010207 (watershed ID 0601)
geographicAreas.description: Hydrologic Unit Code and MDEQ watershed ID given for the watershed.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: The watershed ID number is 0601, and the Hydrologic Unit Code (HUC) code for the watershed is 08010207.

geographicAreas.name: Project target area
geographicAreas.description: The area of about 3,940 acres within the subwatershed, including about 2,167 acres of pasture land, that the 319 project targets for BMPs.
geographicAreas.sourceQuote: This project will target an area in the Bell Creek-West Prong Muddy Creek Subwatershed which is approximately 3,940 acres within the watershed that contains about 2,167 acres of pasture land.
